walkthroughs.body_html:
Run for Your Life — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Run for Your Life brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Run for Your Life.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is actually transferred to the body when you get a vaccine?
options: Antigens (often from weakened, dead, or fragmented pathogens) that train the immune system to make memory cells.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Vaccines inject ready-made antibodies directly into the bloodstream.
Vaccines insert new genes into your DNA permanently.

mcqs.q: What reads the mRNA codons during translation?
options: DNA directly reads the codons on mRNA and adds amino acids.
tRNA molecules carrying specific amino acids — their anticodons pair with mRNA codons at the ribosome.
Ribosomes synthesise amino acids from scratch using the mRNA as a template.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.

mcqs.q: How does a population of organisms become better adapted to its environment over time?
options: Individuals with advantageous heritable variations survive and reproduce more; their alleles increase in frequency over generations.
Individual organisms change during their lifetime in response to their environment and pass the changes on to offspring.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Ribosomes synthesise amino acids from scratch using the mRNA as a template.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Monomer”?
options: Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.
Small repeating subunit that forms polymers, e.g. amino acid, monosaccharide, nucleotide.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Condensation reaction”?
options: Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.
Small repeating subunit that forms polymers, e.g. amino acid, monosaccharide, nucleotide.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Hydrolysis”?
options: Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.
Small repeating subunit that forms polymers, e.g. amino acid, monosaccharide, nucleotide.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ester bond”?
options: Small repeating subunit that forms polymers, e.g. amino acid, monosaccharide, nucleotide.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Glycosidic bond”?
options: Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.
Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Polymer”?
options: Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.
Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.
